## Generic ghost exchange (`SyncOptions`) {#sec-ch03-exchange}

A ghost exchange is the fill of a block's ghost cells from the interior cells of its neighbours; a halo exchange is
the same operation under another name. Every ghost that is not at a physical face (@sec-ch03-physfaces) is filled
by an exchange. A sync packs, for each direction with a neighbour, the interior slab next to that face into a send
buffer, moves the buffers (between processes through the communication backend, @sec-ch14-backends, with the
message matching and in-process copies of @sec-ch14-msgmatch), and unpacks each received buffer into the ghost slab
of the same direction. On the `slab` and `cubed` layouts the four $x_2$-$x_3$ ghost corners come from the diagonal
neighbour when there is one; where there is none, and everywhere on the cubed sphere, they are synthesised from the
two edge strips. The per-stage sync exchanges the conserved variables of the hydro and, when there are scalars, of
the scalar; @sec-ch03-synctype lists the other syncs. On the cubed sphere the same steps run with interpolation
across panel edges (@sec-ch03-csinterp). This section states what a ghost holds; how the transfer is carried, and
how an in-stage exchange becomes a cut of a captured segment, is the subject of @sec-ch14.

`MeshBlockImpl::exchange` orchestrates the block sync through its layout; `LayoutImpl` owns the
packing, the remote exchange and the finalisation, including `LayoutImpl::exchange_remote`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange >}},
{{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::exchange_remote >}}).

Local symbols: $q^{\mathrm{c}}_{k,j}$ a synthesised corner ghost value; $q^{\mathrm{L}}$ and
$q^{\mathrm{B}}$ the ghost strips left ($x_2$ side) and below ($x_3$ side) of a corner, with $j_0$, $k_0$ their
first ghost column and row next to the corner; $\iota_a\in\{-1,0,1\}$ the direction of a neighbour along $x_a$, in cells (the code's `offset`).

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** For each neighbour across a face, copy its interior slab of width $n_g$ into this block's ghost slab;
fill each $x_2$-$x_3$ ghost corner from the diagonal neighbour, or, where there is none and on the cubed sphere, as
the mean of the two adjacent ghost strips (@eq-ch03-exchange-corner).

**Data.** In: the neighbours' interior cells. Out: ghost slabs and corners, in the units of the synced variables
(conserved by default).

**Placement.** Every block sync: the per-stage conserved sync, the primitive and scalar syncs.

**Activation.** `SyncOptions` (`type`, `skip_corner`, `interpolate`, `dim`, `phyid`, phase flags); default conserved
variables, corners by the layout's corner rule, no interpolation.

**Guarantee / limits.** Face and diagonal copies are exact; the synthesised corner is a convention, exact on a
constant and first order on a gradient.

**Evidence.** `test_exchange`, `test_mesh_exchange_python`, `test_periodic_corners_python`,
`test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange_python` (pass at the pin); check `[C15]`.
:::

### Derivation

The face and diagonal exchanges are copies and need no derivation. The synthesised corner is a convention, stated
here. With $\iota_a$ the direction of a neighbour along $x_a$, and with the left ghost strip $q^{\mathrm{L}}$ (offset
$\iota_2 = -1$) and the bottom strip $q^{\mathrm{B}}$ (offset $\iota_3 = -1$), the lower-left corner ghost at $(k, j)$ is

$$
q^{\mathrm{c}}_{k,j} = \tfrac12\left(q^{\mathrm{L}}_{k_0,\,j} + q^{\mathrm{B}}_{k,\,j_0}\right),
$$ {#eq-ch03-exchange-corner}

that is, the mean of the left strip's value in the same $x_2$ column at the row next to the corner and the bottom
strip's value in the same $x_3$ row at the column next to the corner. @eq-ch03-exchange-corner and its three mirror
images are `synthesize` inside `fill_corners` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::fill_corners >}}). It
reproduces a constant field; for a field with a gradient it is a first-order fill, because both terms are read up to
$n_g$ cells away from the corner cell. The check evaluates @eq-ch03-exchange-corner on every corner ghost of an
$n_g = 3$ block: a constant field is reproduced to exactly zero, and on $q = \alpha + \beta x_2 + \gamma x_3$ the
error halves at each refinement (measured order 1.00, 1.00) and stays under the closed-form bound
$n_g(\Delta x_2|\beta| + \Delta x_3|\gamma|)/2$, with $\Delta x_2 = \Delta x_3$ on the check's grid (`[C15]`).[^exc-c15]

Which corners are synthesised is the layout's corner rule, `CornerRule` ({{< code src/layout/layout.hpp CornerRule >}}):
`diagonal` on `slab` and `cubed`, where a corner with a diagonal neighbour (a periodic image included) is exchanged
like a face and only the others are synthesised; `synthesized` on the cubed sphere
({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.hpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl >}}), where a panel corner has no single diagonal
neighbour and every corner is synthesised.

[^exc-c15]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C15]`; a numpy port of the corner synthesis of `LayoutImpl::fill_corners` at the pin, CPU, double;
    Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

Slabs are addressed by the offset $(\iota_3, \iota_2, \iota_1)$, the direction of the neighbour in cells along
each axis (count); `get_buffer_id` maps an offset to one of 9 buffers (27 on `cubed`, the only layout that
exchanges in $x_1$). The sent slab is the $n_g$-wide interior next to the face; the received slab is the ghost zone
across it. `for_each_direction` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::for_each_direction >}}) lists the
offsets of a sync: with `skip_corner` (the default) it keeps the face offsets and, under the `diagonal` rule, the four
$x_2$-$x_3$ corners; offsets that involve $x_1$ and another axis are never exchanged. The `dim` option restricts a
sync to one direction (used for face states, @sec-ch03-cslrsync). Physical faces are skipped (`_skips_direction`).
`fill_corners` runs at the end of `finalize` when corners are skipped and the sync is not one phase of a split; for
a split cubed-sphere sync `exchange` runs it once after both phases. The per-stage sync runs at the start of each
stage, before reconstruction reads the ghosts. @fig-ch03-exchange-stencil shows the slabs and buffer ids.

```{python}

#| fig-alt: "A block in the centre of a three by three arrangement, numbered 0 to 8, with arrows from the four face neighbours and the corners marked as diagonal or synthesised."
```

: Code map of the generic exchange. {#tbl-ch03-exchange-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-exchange-code):

1. `exchange_ghost_zones` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}) calls
   `exchange_state`, which syncs `hydro_u` as conserved with interpolation on, then `scalar_s` as scalar
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_state >}}).
2. `exchange` takes the two-phase branch on a subdivided cubed sphere
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange >}}), otherwise it calls `_exchange_once`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_exchange_once >}}). That runs the three phases in turn:
   `begin_exchange` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::begin_exchange >}}), `launch_exchange`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::launch_exchange >}}), whose host step is an exchange cut
   of a captured segment (@sec-ch14), and `finalize_exchange`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize_exchange >}}).
3. `serialize` copies each interior slab into the cached send buffer of its `get_buffer_id`
   ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::serialize >}}).
4. `finalize` waits on the messages, calls `deserialize` and then `fill_corners` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::finalize >}}).

**How to use it.** There is no YAML key. The exchange follows from the layout and the boundary names
(@sec-ch03-layouts, @sec-ch03-physfaces), and each caller sets `SyncOptions` in C++. The per-stage sync is
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_state >}}):

```cpp
  SyncOptions opts;
  opts.interpolate(true).type(type);
  Variables sync_vars;
  sync_vars[hydro] = vars.at(hydro);
  exchange(sync_vars, opts);
  if (pscalar->nvar() > 0) {
    opts.type(kScalar);
    sync_vars.clear();
    sync_vars[scalar] = vars.count(scalar) ? vars.at(scalar) : torch::Tensor();
    exchange(sync_vars, opts);
  }
```

Corners without a diagonal neighbour are synthesised by @eq-ch03-exchange-corner in `fill_corners`
({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::fill_corners >}}):

```cpp
  auto synthesize = [&](int dy, int dx) {
    std::tuple<int, int, int> corner(dy, dx, 0);
    if (corner_rule() == CornerRule::diagonal &&
        !_skips_direction(pmb, corner) && neighbor_rank(iloc, corner) >= 0)
      return;
    auto sub = pmb->part(corner, PartOptions().exterior(true));
    auto sub_x2 = pmb->part({0, dx, 0}, PartOptions().exterior(true));
    auto sub_x3 = pmb->part({dy, 0, 0}, PartOptions().exterior(true));
    for (auto& [name, var] : vars) {
      auto var_x2 = var.index(sub_x2).select(-3, dy < 0 ? 0 : -1).unsqueeze(-3);
      auto var_x3 = var.index(sub_x3).select(-2, dx < 0 ? 0 : -1).unsqueeze(-2);
      var.index_put_(sub, 0.5 * (var_x2 + var_x3));
    }
  };
```

Nothing is refused: a face without a neighbour keeps its boundary function.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_mesh_exchange_python` | each ghost of a $2\times2$ slab in one process equals its neighbour's payload | exact | integer payloads |
| `test_periodic_corners_python` | on a domain periodic in $x_2$ and $x_3$ every corner ghost equals the periodic image of its interior cell, after initialisation and after one stage; slab 1 block, slab $2\times2$, `cubed` $2\times2\times2$ | exact (count of wrong cells is 0) | the diagonal copy |
| `test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange_python` | a uniform radial velocity crosses every panel edge unchanged | $10^{-12}$ abs. $+ 10^{-12}$ rel. | round-off of the frame rotations |
| `test_exchange` | ghosts hold the neighbour's payload, two processes | value bounds | payloads identify the sender |

: Tests of the generic exchange. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-exchange-tests}

The slab check, in the top-level script `test_mesh_exchange.py`, is the final `torch.all` comparison of each ghost
with the rank `neighbor_rank` names ({{< code tests/test_mesh_exchange.py >}}). The corner check counts the corner
cells that differ from their periodic image by global cell index ({{< code tests/test_periodic_corners.py >}}); its
header records that before the diagonal rule all 36 corner cells of one slab block and all 144 of a $2\times2$ slab
were wrong. The radial-velocity check sets `ABS_TOL` and `REL_TOL` ({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange.py REL_TOL >}}, {{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange.py ABS_TOL >}})
and compares the worst ghost error against them with `ideal_match`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange.py main >}}). The two-process case uses `ghosts_match_expected`
({{< code tests/test_exchange.cpp ghosts_match_expected >}}). The Python tests run in one process;
`test_exchange.release` runs on two processes with gloo. At the pin all four pass.[^exc-run] No test checks the
synthesised corners of the cubed sphere.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Corners that involve $x_1$ (blocks split in $x_1$ on `cubed`) are never exchanged or synthesised.
- Cubed-sphere corners are always synthesised, first order on a gradient.
:::

At a physical $x_1$ wall such corners are rewritten by the corner refresh (@sec-ch03-cornerrefresh); at an internal
$x_1$ seam they keep stale values (read from the code; not measured). No dimension-split stencil reads them; a
cross-derivative operator could. The face-flux covariance does not read a stale $x_1$-seam corner for an interior
cell: before its $x_1$ differences it relays the one neighbouring face-state row across an $x_1$ seam over the full
transverse extent with `Exchange::x1_rows` ({{< code src/layout/exchange.cpp Exchange::x1_rows >}},
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::_flux_covariance >}}); unused outer ghost rows can still hold
unrefreshed corners when $n_g > 1$ (read from the code; not measured). The switch combinations that are tested are
listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
